items.title: Tracking water use on construction sites
items.description: Water meters were read by hand. With LoRaWAN, GPS, and a dashboard, project managers now see usage live, without walking the site.

treepin.context: The city of Maldegem manages thousands of trees spread across its territory. Periodic inspections are legally required and determine maintenance, safety, and liability.
treepin.problem: Inspecting trees meant climbing, photos, and loose Excel files. There was no central overview or history per tree, and each inspection cost between €50 and €150.
treepin.approach: We mapped out what data already existed — location, species, last inspection — and where it broke down: everything lived on paper or in isolated files, none of it searchable or tied to a map.
treepin.solution: A GIS-native app with mobile field entry. Inspectors enter data on-site, everything syncs automatically to a central map. Follow-up actions get prioritized based on risk.
treepin.outcome: The city of Maldegem now digitizes tree inspections structurally. Cost per inspection dropped from €50–150 to €10–30, and the city has, for the first time, an up-to-date overview of its entire tree stock.

tagalong.context: Architecture firms work in SketchUp with hundreds of objects and tags per project — materials, phasing, disciplines.
tagalong.problem: Tags were kept in sync by hand, disconnected from the model. With every change, the tag structure drifted, and team members worked off outdated information.
tagalong.approach: We looked at how tag data related to the model itself and where the sync broke down: there was no link between what lived in the model and what the team saw in reports or exports.
tagalong.solution: A SketchUp plugin connected to a web backoffice, with real-time tag sync. Teams see the same up-to-date structure, with exports to Excel, PDF, and web.
tagalong.outcome: Design studios now use Tagalong for tag management across multiple projects at once — around 90% faster than the previous, manual approach.

iot-water-meters.context: Construction sites install temporary water meters for billing and usage tracking.
iot-water-meters.problem: Meter readings were taken by hand — error-prone, time-consuming, and often the source of billing disputes.
iot-water-meters.approach: We looked at what data was already available per connection and how it could be collected automatically with minimal hardware, without sending someone on-site every time.
iot-water-meters.solution: LoRaWAN sensors connected to GPS and a cloud dashboard. Project managers see usage per location in real time, without walking the site.
iot-water-meters.outcome: Beta tested on 3 construction sites. Within the first month: fewer billing disputes and faster invoice turnaround.

about.bio: Focus First is a digital lab where we digitalize processes and turn ideas into working solutions. We connect all digital tools into one unified system that brings your idea to life — databases, payment processors, data platforms, whatever your project needs. With a hands-on approach: start small, get something working fast, refine from there. We understand how tools work together and build projects that grow as your needs do.
